info.title: Mbooks API
info.description:
C++ (Drogon) API for Mbooks: books, pages, PDF import, table of contents, comments, orders and payments.

Every JSON response is wrapped: `{ "success": true, "data": … }` or `{ "success": false, "error": { "message", "details"? } }`.

Request bodies reject unknown fields (400).

**Rate limits** (429 with a Retry-After header): every logged-in user gets 120 requests a minute in total; login, sign-up, token refresh, comments, PDF uploads and image signatures have their own limits, listed on each route. Limits are per user or per email, never per IP address.

post.description: Limited to 5 attempts per email per 15 minutes (429).

200.description: New access token **and** a new refresh token (use the new one next time), plus the user

post.description:
Swap a refresh token for new tokens without logging in again. Call it when a request gets 401 because the access token expired (JWT_ACCESS_EXPIRATION, e.g. 15m); the refresh token itself lasts JWT_REFRESH_EXPIRATION (e.g. 7d).

The user is loaded from the database, so a deleted account can't refresh, and a changed email or role is in the new tokens.

401 when the refresh token is invalid, expired, an access token, or the account no longer exists: send the user to log in.

201.description: Created. A welcome email and default settings are created in the background.

post.description: Limited to 30 sign-ups per minute across everyone (429).
Any logged-in user. The creator becomes the book's owner.

post.summary: Get a signed Cloudinary upload for a cover
post.description: 1. Call this. 2. POST the image (`file`) plus every entry of `fields` as multipart/form-data to `upload_url` (straight to Cloudinary). 3. Send Cloudinary's `public_id` as `cover` when creating or updating the book. Cover and image signatures together are limited to 60 per user per hour (429).

delete.description: Book owner or admin. Its pages, table of contents and comments are deleted too.

202.description: Accepted. Watch progress on the WebSocket in `ws_url`.

413.description: PDF too large (PDF_MAX_MB, 20 MB by default)

post.description: Book owner or admin. The PDF's text, headings, pictures and outline replace **all** the book's pages and table of contents. Problems with the PDF itself (password protected, unreadable) end the job as `failed`, reported on the WebSocket. A PDF longer than PDF_MAX_PAGES (2000) imports its first 2000 pages. Runs in the background; only one PDF per book at a time (409 while one is processing). Page 1 becomes the book's cover if it looks like one and the book has none; printed contents pages are removed when the PDF has an outline. Limited to 5 uploads per user per hour (429). The finished job's `warnings` say what was left out.

post.summary: Get a signed upload for an image in the page builder
post.description:
Book owner or admin. For adding a picture to a page by hand, or replacing a figure the PDF import got wrong.

1. Call this. 2. POST the image (`file`) plus every entry of `fields` as multipart/form-data to `upload_url` (straight to Cloudinary; JPG, PNG or WebP, resized to fit 1600×1600). 3. Insert `{"type":"image","attrs":{"src": url}}` into the page and save it as usual.

Images live in the book's folder on Cloudinary, so a later PDF import (which replaces every page) removes them too. Cover and image signatures together are limited to 60 per user per hour (429).

put.description: Book owner or admin. Entries are stored in the order sent.

post.description: Limited to 10 per minute per user (429).

delete.description: The comment's author, the book's owner, or an admin.

get.description:
**WebSocket**, not a normal GET. Connect with `ws://` / `wss://`.

Browsers can't send an Authorization header on a WebSocket, so the access token goes in the query string.

The server sends a `JobStatus` JSON text message straight away and on every change, then closes the socket (code 1000) once the job is `completed` or `failed`. A bad token, an unknown job or someone else's job gets one `{"status":"error","error":"…"}` message and close code 1008.

```js
const ws = new WebSocket(`wss://api.example.com${ws_url}&token=${accessToken}`);
ws.onmessage = (e) => console.log(JSON.parse(e.data));
```

parameters.name: token
parameters.description: Access token (same as the Bearer token)

101.description: Switching protocols. Messages are JobStatus objects.

post.description: Records the payment and adds the book to the user's library.

400.description: Validation failed (see error.details) or bad input

409.description: Conflict (already exists, or a PDF is already processing)

429.description: Rate limited. Wait the number of seconds in the Retry-After header and try again.

Retry-After.description: Seconds until another request is allowed

password.description: Needs an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter and a special character

refresh_token.description: The refresh_token from login or from the previous refresh

price.description: In major units (naira, dollars), 2 decimal places

cover_url.description: Only present when the book has a cover

owner_id.description: The user who created the book. Null for books created before owners existed

cover.description: public_id returned by Cloudinary after uploading with a cover signature

UpdateBook.description: Every field optional; omitted fields stay the same

cover.description: public_id returned by Cloudinary after uploading with a cover signature

fields.description: Send all of these as form fields together with `file` to upload_url. Valid for 1 hour.
Send all of these as form fields together with `file` to upload_url. Valid for 1 hour, for this one image.

url.description: Use as the image node's `src` once the upload succeeds

content.description:
A TipTap / ProseMirror document as a JSON string: `JSON.parse` it and pass it to the editor; save with `JSON.stringify(editor.getJSON())`.

Node types: `paragraph`, `heading` (attrs.level 1-3), `text` (marks: `bold`, `italic`) and `image` (attrs: `src`, `alt`, `title`). PDF imports put pictures, drawn figures and picture pages in `image` nodes, so the editor needs StarterKit plus `@tiptap/extension-image`.

ws_url.description: Open a WebSocket to this path, adding &token=<access token>

JobStatus.description: Sent as a WebSocket text message on every change

status.description: `error` only for a rejected connection (bad token, unknown job)

warnings.description: Filled when the job completes: what was left out or changed, e.g. pages or pictures over the limit, removed table-of-contents pages, page 1 used as the cover
example: Page 1 looked like a cover, so it was removed from the pages and set as the book's cover
120 pictures were left out: the limit is 300 per book
